search.objective: minimum observed two-norm condition number; density and transform complexity recorded but not scalarized

decision.selected: replace the catalogue basis by the recorded trial-668 integral basis for the next transformer and calibration design pass
decision.gain: the adversarial one-percent inverse-metric tolerance relaxes by the same factor 42.98, from 3.11e-7 to 1.34e-5
decision.tradeoff: the reduced Gram matrix has four more nonzero off-diagonal pairs, and the coordinate transform is moderately dense; condition number improved without a sparsity improvement
decision.next: factor the winning Gram matrix, quantify its transformer network, and search the Pareto frontier rather than treating condition number alone as the design objective

established: a verified GL(24,Z)-equivalent Leech basis in the declared finite scan reduces the recorded-basis condition number by a factor of about 43 while retaining 24 minimum-norm-four basis vectors
boundary: This is the best observed candidate in a finite deterministic heuristic scan, not a proof of global or local optimality. Euclidean conditioning is a hardware-coordinate criterion rather than a lattice invariant, and the improvement does not establish a realizable layout, parasitic tolerance or the Leech infrared phase.
